the-lion-king.title: The Lion King
the-lion-king.notes: The Lion King is one of Broadway's longest-running and highest-grossing shows, opening in November 1997 and still running. It is widely acknowledged as a mega-hit. However, none of the evidence gathered contains explicit figures for capitalization, weekly running costs, or a specific recoupment date. The theatregold.com source references a $9 billion gross figure in its keywords, but no usable financial detail was extractable from the evidence provided. Designation as Miracle is based on the show's well-known status as a decades-long phenomenon, but specific financial data cannot be cited from these sources.
the-lion-king.archivedDetail: Only source is a theatregold.com cost explainer with no recoupment date or report. commercial.json the-lion-king already records recouped:true (Miracle, 1999 estimate); nothing new to apply.

moulin-rouge.title: Moulin Rouge! The Musical
moulin-rouge.capitalizationSource: nytix.com article listing top 10 most expensive Broadway shows, states '$28 Million' capitalization for Moulin Rouge! The Musical
moulin-rouge.recoupedSource: BroadwayWorld article dated 2023-07-31 titled 'MOULIN ROUGE! THE MUSICAL Recoups on Broadway, in the West End & in Australia'; Deadline article from 2023-07 referencing recoupment; nytix.com also confirms recoupment
moulin-rouge.notes: Moulin Rouge! The Musical opened July 25, 2019 and is scheduled to close August 30, 2026 — a roughly 7-year run. It was capitalized at $28 million per trade reporting, won 10 Tony Awards including Best Musical, and recouped its Broadway investment in July 2023 (also recouping simultaneously in the West End and Australia). While a strong commercial hit, its ~7-year run falls short of the decade-plus phenomenon threshold for a Miracle designation, making Windfall the appropriate classification.
moulin-rouge.archivedDetail: Duplicate. commercial.json moulin-rouge already cites Broadway News (2023-08-03) quoting the production 'recouped its investment in November 2022'; the 2023-07 date here is the announcement date, not a correction.

leopoldstadt-2022.capitalizationSource: Washington Post described Leopoldstadt as roughly an $8 million Broadway production and said it initially had to raise more than $8 million. ([washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/theater-dance/2022/09/29/tom-stoppard-leopoldstadt-broadway/?utm_source=openai))
leopoldstadt-2022.recoupedSource: A 2026 profile/interview with producer Catherine Adler says Leopoldstadt recouped its investment. ([palmerpb.com](https://palmerpb.com/2026/06/04/nine-tonys-and-counting-a-conversation-with-catherine-adler/?utm_source=openai))
leopoldstadt-2022.notes: I used the direct contemporaneous ~$8 million budget estimate rather than back-solving from the later $3 million NYC tax credit award, because the credit is a subsidy and does not map one-to-one onto original Broadway capitalization. New York tax rules say the credit equals 25% of qualified NYC production expenditures and was capped at $3 million for this opening date; Broadway Journal also reported weekly fixed costs of about $580,000 before royalties, and Playbill’s closing gross page puts total Broadway grosses at $32.7 million. Public sources confirm recoupment, but not the exact month it happened. ([tax.ny.gov](https://www.tax.ny.gov/data/stats/ter/fiscal-year27/cross-article-tax-credits.htm?utm_source=openai))
